title: Efficient LLM Scheduling by Learning to Rank
technique: learning-to-rank predictor of output-length ordering to approximate SJF/SRTF scheduling in vLLM, with starvation prevention

optimized_metrics.evidence: we measure average and p90 per-token latency, which is the per-request latency divided by the output length
reducing the p90 latency of chatbot serving by 2.8×
For offline synthetic generation tasks, we use throughput (requests/second) to indicate request generation speed.
we propose a max_waiting_time fairness metric to evaluate the fairness at per-request level ... This method prevents starvation at a request level, improves max_waiting_time

headline_claim.text: 2.8x lower latency in chatbot serving and 6.5x higher throughput in synthetic data generation

metric_definitions.definition_quote: we measure average and p90 per-token latency, which is the per-request latency divided by the output length
metric_definitions.notes: normalized per-request latency, includes queueing; not TPOT

metric_definitions.definition_quote: For offline synthetic generation tasks, we use throughput (requests/second) to indicate request generation speed.
metric_definitions.notes: requests/s; SDG experiments also measure time to generate 1k requests

metric_definitions.definition_quote: max_waiting_time = max(TTFT,max(TPOT)). Intuitively, it characterizes the maximum time interval between receiving two tokens after the user sends a request to the server.
metric_definitions.notes: TPOT here is used as inter-token gap, i.e. TBT-like

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Kendall's Tau coefficient ... can characterize the correlation between two rankings
metric_definitions.notes: proxy objective for predictor; higher tau -> lower latency

load_regime: request-rate sweep on ShareGPT and LMSYS-Chat-1M (Fig 3), burst of 2k requests (Tab 1), offline fixed-quantity/time-limited synthetic data generation
tradeoff_acknowledged: starvation of long requests; starvation prevention costs <10% (most cases) and <30% (all) latency
extractor_notes: Primary objective is mean latency (SJF/SRTF minimizes average); p90 is headline. Offline SDG throughput is objective of a second use case, and there short responses are preferred. Latency is per-token normalized, not TTFT/TPOT.
